pathway.title: Griffon Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Cash generation is the core credit strength, and it is stable rather than peaking. Operating cash flow from continuing operations was USD 307.37 million, USD 307.79 million and USD 304.87 million in the last three years, and capital expenditure of USD 37.91 million is only 2.05% of revenue. Free cash flow of USD 266.95 million is therefore 58.08% of adjusted EBITDA, is already struck after cash interest of USD 81.08 million and cash taxes of USD 96.04 million, and equals 25.54% of year-end debt, so debt service is not the constraint. Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 72–74; calculation C1; calculation C12

Leverage is moderate but was bought with asset sales, and further deleveraging depends on the cash left after shareholder returns. Net debt of USD 946.66 million (USD 963.55 million pro forma for share repurchases to 2026-11-16) is 2.12x reported EBITDA (2.15x pro forma) and 2.06x issuer-adjusted EBITDA, against 2.0x on the issuer's own credit agreement definition. Adjusted EBITDA fell 0.48% in FY2026, so the fall in debt came mainly from USD 304.38 million of sale proceeds and not from earnings growth. After dividends and buybacks of USD 191.71 million, free cash flow leaves only USD 75.24 million, which would take 12.58 years to repay net debt. Pro forma net debt for the dividend declared on 2026-11-16 is not established because its total payout is not stated. Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54, 65–66, 73; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2

Financial policy is the weakest dimension, because the board's buyback authority is larger than the liquidity that would fund it. Authority of USD 544.80 million is 1.68x year-end liquidity of USD 324.23 million and 2.04x annual free cash flow, so it could not be met from cash on hand. Returns absorbed 96.23% of three-year free cash flow, exceeded it in FY2024 at USD 345.72 million against USD 257.09 million, and no leverage target is stated. The senior notes have limited covenants and the revolver's restricted payment limits are not supplied, so a debt-funded authority would lift net leverage from 2.15x pro forma to about 3.37x. Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 54, 56, 73; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C10

Earnings are stable but their quality is eroding, because price is carrying weaker volume. FY2026 revenue rose 2.95% to USD 1,848.38 million on price and mix of 6% against volume down 3%, yet gross margin slipped to 46.36% from 47.24% and adjusted EBITDA margin to 24.86% from 25.99% in FY2024. Only 16.75% of the added revenue turned into gross profit, because lower volume absorbed less overhead and material costs rose, and raw material costs reach prices with a lag. The final quarter was better: derived adjusted EBITDA rose 4.06% against a 2.13% fall over the first nine months, at a quarterly margin of 26.04%. Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 45–46, 65, 72; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gff-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 58; calculation C4; calculation C5

Demand is discretionary and concentrated, so volume is the variable that matters most, and the fan business is the weaker leg. Residential repair and remodel was 53.34% of revenue and commercial 39.29%. Home Depot and Menards take garage doors on an exclusive basis, hold 8% and 11% of net receivables, and the filing says losing either would be materially adverse. The fan business competes with retailer house brands, is the most exposed to tariffs, and a goodwill and trademark impairment of USD 243.61 million in FY2025 left the trademark with minimal headroom in the auditor's words. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_gff-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 52; 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 10, 19–20, 23, 70, 122–123; calculation C8

Liquidity is adequate and maturities are distant, but most of the liquidity is a revolver whose availability depends on covenant tests that are not supplied. Year-end liquidity of USD 324.23 million includes USD 225.60 million of undrawn revolver, 69.58%, and USD 52.30 million of the cash is held outside the United States; USD 16.89 million of repurchases have followed. Nothing material falls due before the revolver matures in fiscal 2031 and the USD 800.00 million of 6.25% notes in 2034. Run-rate interest on the notes and the drawn revolver is about USD 64.69 million against USD 81.08 million paid in FY2026, which lifts cover to about 6.92x from 5.52x. Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 51, 55–57, 74, 103–105; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6; calculation C9

Asset cover beneath the operating business is thin, so any recovery would rest on enterprise value rather than tangible assets. Goodwill and intangibles of USD 534.86 million exceed shareholders' equity of USD 306.78 million, leaving tangible equity below zero by USD 228.09 million, and USD 355.08 million of joint venture notes and equity, 115.75% of equity, pays no cash interest. The revolver is secured on substantially all domestic assets and USD 260.00 million is drawn, 24.53% of principal debt, ahead of the unsecured notes. Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 55–56, 71–72, 93–95, 103–105; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C8

Ownership helps and event risk offsets it. The company is listed with no sponsor identified, and its board is independent apart from the chief executive, who is also chairman, which removes sponsor extraction risk. It has nevertheless reshaped its portfolio repeatedly since 2018, with the sale or closure of AMES in FY2026 the latest step, and a debt-funded acquisition is the other route to higher leverage that the notes' limited covenants may not restrict. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_gff-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 15, 27; Business & governance (CP-1A)

cells.text: Largest North American maker of residential and commercial garage doors and rolling steel doors, and a leading maker of ceiling fans, sold under the Clopay, IDEAL, Holmes, Cornell, Cookson, Hunter, Casablanca and Jan Fan brands
Two product families on one operating segment, so earnings move with housing and commercial construction activity
Residential repair and remodel 53.34%, commercial 39.29%, residential new construction 7.38% of revenue; about 95% of revenue is in the United States
Over half of revenue depends on remodelling activity, which is discretionary and tied to housing turnover and consumer credit

Exclusive supplier of garage doors to Home Depot and Menards; over 3,000 independent professional installing dealers; 58 distribution centres; Home Depot and Menards were 8% and 11% of net receivables at 2026-09-30 and no customer reached 10% of FY2026 revenue
Two retailers hold material bargaining power and receivable exposure; the filing states that losing either would have a material adverse effect
Revenue rose 3% on price and mix of 6% offset by volume down 3%, driven by residential; gross margin fell to 46.4% from 47.2%
Price carried the year; if retailers resist further increases while volume stays weak, margin and cash flow narrow
Galvanized steel is the principal raw material; sourced finished goods were about 10% of revenue and sourced components about 13% of cost of goods sold; some products come only from China
Steel and tariff swings reach margin with a lag, and the filing says price increases are hard to pass through quickly
Principal factories in Ohio, Pennsylvania and Arizona, distribution in Mississippi and a network of leased centres; about 3,355 employees at 2026-09-30
Manufacturing is concentrated in a few owned plants, so a plant outage would hit supply to the two large retailers
Door demand is strongest in the first and fourth fiscal quarters and fans in the second and third; most revenue is short cycle with shipments inside one year and no backlog figure is disclosed
Short order cycles give little forward visibility, so quarterly cash flow and revolver use swing with the season
AMES hand tools, home organisation and lawn and garden businesses were sold or closed and are now reported as discontinued operations, leaving Building Products as the only operating segment
The business that remains is narrower and higher margin, and the sale terms leave Griffon holding paper from the buyers

runs.text: The first credit strength is stable, capital-light cash generation. Operating cash flow of USD 304.87 million less capital expenditure of USD 37.91 million left free cash flow of USD 266.95 million after interest and taxes, so EBITDA reliably becomes cash and debt service is well supported. Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 72–74; calculation C1

The second credit strength is the repaired debt structure. The term loan was repaid, the 5.75% notes due 2028 were replaced by 6.25% notes due 2034 and the revolver was extended to 2031, so no material principal is due before fiscal 2031 and refinancing pressure is low for several years. Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53, 55–57, 105; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The third credit strength is a falling interest burden. Interest on the new notes and the drawn revolver runs at about USD 64.69 million a year against USD 81.08 million paid in FY2026, which lifts reported EBITDA cover to about 6.92x if earnings hold. Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 55–57, 74; calculation C6

The fourth credit strength is a leading position in garage doors held through exclusive supply to the two largest home-improvement retailers and an installing dealer network. That supports volume and price realisation, although the same relationships create the concentration weakness below. Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9, 20

The first credit weakness is financial policy. The board's repurchase authority of USD 544.80 million is 1.68x year-end liquidity, returns took 96.23% of three-year free cash flow, and the senior notes carry limited covenants, so debt-funded returns could lift net leverage to about 3.37x without any earnings fall. Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 54, 73; calculation C3; calculation C10

The second credit weakness is customer concentration and discretionary demand. Residential repair and remodel is 53.34% of revenue, two retailers hold exclusive garage door supply and 8% and 11% of net receivables, and the filing calls the loss of either materially adverse, so a change in volume or price terms reaches EBITDA quickly. Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 20, 122–123

The third credit weakness is margin erosion under price-led growth. Gross margin slipped to 46.36% from 47.24% and only 16.75% of the added revenue turned into gross profit, which shows cost increases and lower overhead absorption taking the benefit of price. Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45, 72; calculation C4

The fourth credit weakness is thin tangible asset cover. Goodwill and intangibles exceed shareholders' equity and USD 355.08 million of joint venture notes and equity pays no cash interest, so recovery rests on enterprise value and on partners Griffon does not control. Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 71–72, 93–95; calculation C8

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: In fiscal 2026 Griffon turned itself into a pure-play building-products issuer. On 2026-06-09 it combined AMES North America with other businesses into the Veritage Brands joint venture, receiving USD 100.00 million of cash, a USD 161.10 million second-lien paid-in-kind loan and a 43% equity interest carried at USD 118.60 million. On 2026-07-31 it sold AMES Australasia to Griffon ANZ for USD 180.91 million of cash, a paid-in-kind note of AUD 69.3 million (about USD 48.59 million) and a 49% interest carried at USD 20.90 million. AMES U.K. ceased trading on 2026-03-31 and its liquidation was substantially complete at year-end. Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6, 94–95

The refinancing on 2026-08-18 had two parts. Griffon issued USD 800.00 million of 6.25% senior notes due 2034 in a private placement, unsecured and guaranteed by named domestic subsidiaries, and amended and restated its credit agreement to extend the USD 500.00 million revolver from 2028 to 2031 and remove the credit spread adjustment. The new notes and revolver borrowings repaid all USD 974.78 million of the 5.75% senior notes due 2028, and the USD 449.00 million term loan was repaid in full during the year. The new notes have limited covenants while the revolver carries maintenance tests, and the covenant levels are not supplied. Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 53, 55–57, 104–106

After the year-end, on 2026-11-16 the board declared a dividend of USD 0.25 per share payable on 2026-12-16 and added USD 400 million to the repurchase authority, bringing the amount available at 2026-11-17 to USD 544.80 million. These are subsequent events and are not in the year-end figures. Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54

fields.value: Financial foundation for Griffon Corp (issuer gff-50725) as of 2026-11-18, under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: normalised statements for the continuing-operations perimeter, net debt, liquidity, leverage and interest cover, built from the four supplied filings and the Source readiness handoff.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Griffon Corp ended fiscal 2026 at 2.12x net debt to reported EBITDA with no material principal due before fiscal 2031, but the deleveraging came from asset sales while adjusted EBITDA was flat, so creditor protection depends on cash discipline after the disposals.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53, 72, 103–105; calculation C1; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt fell to USD 946.66 million from USD 1,313.26 million a year earlier, helped by USD 304.38 million of disposal proceeds, while dividends and buybacks of USD 191.71 million absorbed most of free cash flow of USD 266.95 million. Pro forma for buybacks to 2026-11-16, net debt is USD 963.55 million, or 2.15x. Cash interest cover is 5.52x and liquidity is USD 324.23 million, but covenant levels are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54, 56, 73–74, 114; calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C11; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage fell sharply in fiscal 2026 and now sits at 2.12x net debt to reported EBITDA (2.15x pro forma for buybacks to 2026-11-16) and 2.06x on issuer-adjusted EBITDA, against a compliance figure of 2.0x that uses principal net debt and adds stock-based compensation. The mechanism was disposal proceeds of USD 304.38 million from the AMES businesses, equal to 83.03% of the USD 366.60 million fall in net debt, with the term loan repaid in full and the 2028 notes refinanced by new notes and revolver borrowings. It was not earnings growth: adjusted EBITDA slipped 0.48% against a year earlier. The earlier ratios of 6.06x for FY2025 and 2.57x at June 2026 are not a like-for-like trend, because that debt was carried by the whole group including businesses since disposed of.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53, 65–66, 72; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gff-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 60; calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C12; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating earnings are stable but margins are eroding. Revenue rose 2.95% to USD 1,848.38 million on price and mix, offset by lower residential volume, gross margin slipped to 46.36% from 47.24%, and adjusted EBITDA margin has fallen in each of the last two years to 24.86%. Lower volume absorbs less overhead and material costs rose, so price increases are carrying the earnings that creditors rely on for coverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is strong and consistent. Operating cash flow from continuing operations was USD 304.87 million and free cash flow USD 266.95 million, 58.08% of adjusted EBITDA, with capital expenditure of only USD 37.91 million. Shareholder returns took 71.81% of free cash flow, which leaves a cushion but is discretionary and can be raised: the board added USD 400 million of repurchase authority on 2026-11-16.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 54, 73; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest burden is falling but not yet at its run rate. Cash interest of USD 81.08 million gave cover of 5.52x, yet it includes interest on debt that was repaid in August 2026, and the issuer states annual interest on the new notes of about USD 50 million. The new notes carry 6.25% against 5.75% on the retired notes, so the cost per dollar of debt rose while the amount of debt fell.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate but conditional. Cash of USD 98.63 million plus revolver availability of USD 225.60 million gives USD 324.23 million, down from USD 584.72 million at 2025-09-30 because USD 260.00 million of the revolver is drawn, and USD 52.30 million of the cash is held outside the United States. The revolver matures in 2031 and the notes in 2034, so there is no refinancing event inside the next four fiscal years, but availability is subject to maintenance tests whose levels are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Griffon retains USD 215.58 million of related-party second-lien paid-in-kind notes and USD 139.50 million of equity-method investments from the joint ventures. Neither has a quoted price in the filing, so they add to asset cover only if they can be monetised.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is cash generation. Free cash flow of USD 266.95 million was 25.54% of year-end debt, interest is falling as the term loan and the 2028 notes are replaced, and shareholder returns of USD 191.71 million were covered by free cash flow, so debt could fall further without asset sales. The view would soften if adjusted EBITDA stabilises and buybacks stay below free cash flow for another year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54, 73; calculation C7; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would harden if EBITDA keeps falling in step with margins, if buybacks funded partly by the revolver push net debt above the pro forma figure, or if the joint venture notes prove hard to collect. Pro forma net leverage after repurchases to 2026-11-16 is 2.15x, and every further USD 100 million of buybacks adds about 0.22x on reported EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business, ownership, governance and transaction fact pack for Griffon Corp (issuer gff-50725) as of 2026-11-18, under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the continuing building-products business, its owners and governance, financial policy and the 2026 disposals and refinancing, built from the four supplied filings and the Source readiness handoff.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Griffon Corp is a listed building-products maker with no sponsor identified, so creditor risk lies in board-controlled financial policy: shareholder returns absorbed 96.23% of three-year free cash flow and 55.42% of the disposal consideration came as non-cash claims on the buyers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 53–54, 94–95; calculation C5; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The continuing business is two product families, garage doors and ceiling fans, sold largely through two home-improvement retailers, with residential repair and remodel at 53.34% of revenue and a gross margin of 46.36% against 27.69% in the divested AMES business. The board alone sets buybacks, with USD 544.80 million of authority available at 2026-11-17, about 2.04x a year of free cash flow. Overall sponsor and governance risk is medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 20, 54, 122–123; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The remaining business is more profitable but narrower, and it leans on two customers. Home Depot and Menards buy garage doors on an exclusive basis, hold 8% and 11% of net receivables, and the filing says losing either would be materially adverse; over half of revenue is repair and remodel work that follows housing turnover and consumer credit. In fiscal 2026 price and mix of 6% offset a 3% volume fall, so earnings rest on retailers accepting price increases while demand is soft.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The disposals cut debt but left creditors holding junior paper. Of the headline consideration at recorded values, 44.58% was cash and 55.42% was PIK notes and equity in the buyers' vehicles. At year-end Griffon carried USD 215.58 million of PIK notes and USD 139.50 million of equity stakes, equal to 115.75% of its shareholders' equity and 20.65% of total assets. The PIK interest brings no cash, the Veritage loan is second lien, and Veritage's liabilities were 83.81% of its assets three weeks after formation, so recovery depends on partners Griffon does not control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 71, 93–95; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor or controlling holder is identified, so the risk is board policy rather than sponsor extraction. The company is listed and employees own about 8% through the ESOP, but the annual report does not list its largest holders because that information sits in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so a concentrated holder cannot be ruled out. No management, monitoring or advisory fees appear in the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns are the main financial-policy risk. Over three years Griffon returned USD 760.40 million through dividends and buybacks against free cash flow of USD 790.15 million, or 96.23%, and 71.81% of free cash flow in fiscal 2026. Returns fell each year and have been covered by free cash flow since fiscal 2025, but the repurchase authority of USD 544.80 million equals 2.04x a year of free cash flow, so debt-funded buybacks could undo the deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54, 73; calculation C5; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The board is mostly independent but the chair and chief executive are one person. All directors except the chief executive are independent, a lead independent director and four committees operate, and the auditor gives clean opinions on the statements and on internal control. That supports monitoring, yet the same board sets dividends and buybacks at its discretion and the legal limits on them are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The refinancing was creditor-friendly on maturity but thin on protection. The term loan was repaid, the 2028 notes were replaced by 2034 notes and the revolver was extended to 2031, which removes near-term refinancing pressure. The new notes carry limited covenants and a higher coupon, so the revolver's maintenance tests are the main restraint on distributions and the covenant levels are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Event risk persists despite the pure-play label. Griffon divested specialty plastics in 2018 and its defense electronics business in 2022, bought CornellCookson, ClosetMaid and Hunter Fan, and in fiscal 2026 sold or closed AMES; the 2025 annual report said it intended to diversify further through acquisitions. A debt-funded acquisition would raise leverage, and the senior notes have limited covenants, so the main contractual protection is the revolver, whose test levels are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Legal and environmental claims are unquantified. The filing treats a Memphis site liability as probable without an amount, an environmental study at a New York site is due in 2027 and a New Jersey information request was received and answered, and management says none is expected to be material. For creditors this is a possible cash call with no number attached.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that policy has been creditor-aligned in practice: no sponsor drains cash, returns fell each year and were covered by free cash flow in fiscal 2025 and 2026, the term loan was repaid in full, maturities were extended to 2031 and 2034, and the board is independent apart from the chief executive. The PIK notes and equity are a minority of total assets at 20.65% and carry 10% PIK interest. On this evidence the risk level could be lower than medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would turn adverse if repurchases are funded from the revolver so that debt rises, if the joint ventures show losses or capitalise rather than pay interest, if a holder concentration or activist campaign emerges, or if the indenture and credit agreement show wide capacity for distributions. It would improve if the executed documents show tight restricted payment limits and the venture accounts show service of the notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so shareholder concentration, director holdings and incentive design are not established; this could overturn the conclusion that no controlling holder or sponsor exists.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The notes indenture and credit agreement are not supplied, so legal capacity for distributions, investments and asset transfers is not established; the conclusion on buyback risk rests on observed behaviour and the filing's own summary only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The ventures' financial statements and debt terms are not supplied beyond one summarised balance sheet, so the recoverability of the PIK notes and equity is not tested; the asset cover conclusion cannot be firmed up from these filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In fiscal 2026 Griffon turned itself into a pure-play building-products issuer. On 2026-06-09 it combined AMES North America with other businesses into the Veritage Brands joint venture, receiving USD 100.00 million of cash, a USD 161.10 million second-lien paid-in-kind loan and a 43% equity interest carried at USD 118.60 million. On 2026-07-31 it sold AMES Australasia to Griffon ANZ for USD 180.91 million of cash, a paid-in-kind note of AUD 69.3 million (about USD 48.59 million) and a 49% interest carried at USD 20.90 million. AMES U.K. ceased trading on 2026-03-31 and its liquidation was substantially complete at year-end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The refinancing on 2026-08-18 had two parts. Griffon issued USD 800.00 million of 6.25% senior notes due 2034 in a private placement, unsecured and guaranteed by named domestic subsidiaries, and amended and restated its credit agreement to extend the USD 500.00 million revolver from 2028 to 2031 and remove the credit spread adjustment. The new notes and revolver borrowings repaid all USD 974.78 million of the 5.75% senior notes due 2028, and the USD 449.00 million term loan was repaid in full during the year. The new notes have limited covenants while the revolver carries maintenance tests, and the covenant levels are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After the year-end, on 2026-11-16 the board declared a dividend of USD 0.25 per share payable on 2026-12-16 and added USD 400 million to the repurchase authority, bringing the amount available at 2026-11-17 to USD 544.80 million. These are subsequent events and are not in the year-end figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module status: Ready with Limitations. No executed legal documents, proxy statement, sponsor materials or fee disclosures are supplied, which limits the legal-capacity and ownership tests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No creditor-adverse conduct is documented in the sources read: no uptier, drop-down, priming, non-pro-rata exchange, covenant waiver, collateral release for a creditor-adverse purpose, or distribution during stress appears in the filings. The August 2026 amendment extended the revolver maturity and removed a spread adjustment, and the guarantees of two AMES subsidiaries were released on their sale.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by board-controlled shareholder returns and the non-cash disposal consideration, because the board can raise distributions or fund buybacks from the revolver while the paper from the buyers produces no cash, which implies that leverage and asset cover depend on policy discipline rather than on a sponsor's balance sheet. Countervailing evidence is an independent board, audited reporting, a lengthened maturity profile and returns that fell each year and were covered by free cash flow in fiscal 2025 and 2026. Further analysis requires the executed credit agreement and indenture, the proxy statement and the venture financial statements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Griffon Corp (issuer gff-50725) as of 2026-11-18, under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the continuing building-products business as reported at 2026-09-30, built from the four supplied filings and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance results. It gives no rating, recovery estimate, relative-value label or position size.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Griffon is a cash-generative building-products credit of adequate quality, and the main risk to creditors is discretionary shareholder returns rather than operations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 54, 73; calculation C3; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt of USD 946.66 million (USD 963.55 million pro forma for share repurchases to 2026-11-16) is 2.12x reported EBITDA (2.15x pro forma), free cash flow is USD 266.95 million and no material principal falls due before fiscal 2031. If the whole USD 544.80 million buyback authority were debt-funded, net leverage would reach about 3.37x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 54, 56, 73, 103–105; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is the core credit strength, and it is stable rather than peaking. Operating cash flow from continuing operations was USD 307.37 million, USD 307.79 million and USD 304.87 million in the last three years, and capital expenditure of USD 37.91 million is only 2.05% of revenue. Free cash flow of USD 266.95 million is therefore 58.08% of adjusted EBITDA, is already struck after cash interest of USD 81.08 million and cash taxes of USD 96.04 million, and equals 25.54% of year-end debt, so debt service is not the constraint.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 72–74; calculation C1; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is moderate but was bought with asset sales, and further deleveraging depends on the cash left after shareholder returns. Net debt of USD 946.66 million (USD 963.55 million pro forma for share repurchases to 2026-11-16) is 2.12x reported EBITDA (2.15x pro forma) and 2.06x issuer-adjusted EBITDA, against 2.0x on the issuer's own credit agreement definition. Adjusted EBITDA fell 0.48% in FY2026, so the fall in debt came mainly from USD 304.38 million of sale proceeds and not from earnings growth. After dividends and buybacks of USD 191.71 million, free cash flow leaves only USD 75.24 million, which would take 12.58 years to repay net debt. Pro forma net debt for the dividend declared on 2026-11-16 is not established because its total payout is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54, 65–66, 73; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the weakest dimension, because the board's buyback authority is larger than the liquidity that would fund it. Authority of USD 544.80 million is 1.68x year-end liquidity of USD 324.23 million and 2.04x annual free cash flow, so it could not be met from cash on hand. Returns absorbed 96.23% of three-year free cash flow, exceeded it in FY2024 at USD 345.72 million against USD 257.09 million, and no leverage target is stated. The senior notes have limited covenants and the revolver's restricted payment limits are not supplied, so a debt-funded authority would lift net leverage from 2.15x pro forma to about 3.37x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 54, 56, 73; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are stable but their quality is eroding, because price is carrying weaker volume. FY2026 revenue rose 2.95% to USD 1,848.38 million on price and mix of 6% against volume down 3%, yet gross margin slipped to 46.36% from 47.24% and adjusted EBITDA margin to 24.86% from 25.99% in FY2024. Only 16.75% of the added revenue turned into gross profit, because lower volume absorbed less overhead and material costs rose, and raw material costs reach prices with a lag. The final quarter was better: derived adjusted EBITDA rose 4.06% against a 2.13% fall over the first nine months, at a quarterly margin of 26.04%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 45–46, 65, 72; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gff-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 58; calculation C4; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Demand is discretionary and concentrated, so volume is the variable that matters most, and the fan business is the weaker leg. Residential repair and remodel was 53.34% of revenue and commercial 39.29%. Home Depot and Menards take garage doors on an exclusive basis, hold 8% and 11% of net receivables, and the filing says losing either would be materially adverse. The fan business competes with retailer house brands, is the most exposed to tariffs, and a goodwill and trademark impairment of USD 243.61 million in FY2025 left the trademark with minimal headroom in the auditor's words.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate and maturities are distant, but most of the liquidity is a revolver whose availability depends on covenant tests that are not supplied. Year-end liquidity of USD 324.23 million includes USD 225.60 million of undrawn revolver, 69.58%, and USD 52.30 million of the cash is held outside the United States; USD 16.89 million of repurchases have followed. Nothing material falls due before the revolver matures in fiscal 2031 and the USD 800.00 million of 6.25% notes in 2034. Run-rate interest on the notes and the drawn revolver is about USD 64.69 million against USD 81.08 million paid in FY2026, which lifts cover to about 6.92x from 5.52x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 51, 55–57, 74, 103–105; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Asset cover beneath the operating business is thin, so any recovery would rest on enterprise value rather than tangible assets. Goodwill and intangibles of USD 534.86 million exceed shareholders' equity of USD 306.78 million, leaving tangible equity below zero by USD 228.09 million, and USD 355.08 million of joint venture notes and equity, 115.75% of equity, pays no cash interest. The revolver is secured on substantially all domestic assets and USD 260.00 million is drawn, 24.53% of principal debt, ahead of the unsecured notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 55–56, 71–72, 93–95, 103–105; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership helps and event risk offsets it. The company is listed with no sponsor identified, and its board is independent apart from the chief executive, who is also chairman, which removes sponsor extraction risk. It has nevertheless reshaped its portfolio repeatedly since 2018, with the sale or closure of AMES in FY2026 the latest step, and a debt-funded acquisition is the other route to higher leverage that the notes' limited covenants may not restrict.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that the cash flows are stable and the balance sheet has been repaired. Free cash flow was USD 257.09 million, USD 266.10 million and USD 266.95 million over three years, net leverage of 2.12x (2.15x pro forma for repurchases to 2026-11-16) is moderate in absolute terms, run-rate interest cover is about 6.92x, and no material principal is due before fiscal 2031. Returns also fell each year, from USD 345.72 million in FY2024 to USD 191.71 million in FY2026, and were covered by free cash flow in FY2025 and FY2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54, 73–74; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C6; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would soften if the authority is used only from free cash flow so that net debt keeps falling, if the executed documents show tight restricted payment limits, and if adjusted EBITDA margin returns above 25.72%, its FY2025 level. It would harden if repurchases are funded by revolver draws, if volume falls without a price offset, or if the revolver tests sit close to the issuer's own leverage of 2.0x. A further USD 100.00 million of debt-funded buybacks adds about 0.22x to net leverage on reported EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The covenant test levels and restricted payment limits are not supplied, so the conclusion that liquidity is adequate cannot be tied to a breach point, and the revolver's undrawn USD 225.60 million could be smaller than shown if a test binds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The split of revenue and profit between garage doors and ceiling fans is not printed, so the view that the fan business is the weaker leg rests on the FY2025 impairment and the risk disclosures, and a larger fan share than assumed would lower the margin assessment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside and buyback cases are arithmetic on FY2026 figures with stated assumptions, not forecasts, because no management projection or lender case is supplied; they size the exposure but do not date it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The fourth-quarter improvement is derived by subtracting nine-month stubs from audited annual figures and assumes both sit on the same restated perimeter, so it is unaudited and could shift if the stubs were revised; it supports the margin view only as a direction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No rating, market price or peer data is supplied, so the statement that leverage is moderate rests on its absolute level and the issuer's own history, not on comparable leveraged issuers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first credit strength is stable, capital-light cash generation. Operating cash flow of USD 304.87 million less capital expenditure of USD 37.91 million left free cash flow of USD 266.95 million after interest and taxes, so EBITDA reliably becomes cash and debt service is well supported.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second credit strength is the repaired debt structure. The term loan was repaid, the 5.75% notes due 2028 were replaced by 6.25% notes due 2034 and the revolver was extended to 2031, so no material principal is due before fiscal 2031 and refinancing pressure is low for several years.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third credit strength is a falling interest burden. Interest on the new notes and the drawn revolver runs at about USD 64.69 million a year against USD 81.08 million paid in FY2026, which lifts reported EBITDA cover to about 6.92x if earnings hold.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth credit strength is a leading position in garage doors held through exclusive supply to the two largest home-improvement retailers and an installing dealer network. That supports volume and price realisation, although the same relationships create the concentration weakness below.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first credit weakness is financial policy. The board's repurchase authority of USD 544.80 million is 1.68x year-end liquidity, returns took 96.23% of three-year free cash flow, and the senior notes carry limited covenants, so debt-funded returns could lift net leverage to about 3.37x without any earnings fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 54, 73; calculation C3; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second credit weakness is customer concentration and discretionary demand. Residential repair and remodel is 53.34% of revenue, two retailers hold exclusive garage door supply and 8% and 11% of net receivables, and the filing calls the loss of either materially adverse, so a change in volume or price terms reaches EBITDA quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third credit weakness is margin erosion under price-led growth. Gross margin slipped to 46.36% from 47.24% and only 16.75% of the added revenue turned into gross profit, which shows cost increases and lower overhead absorption taking the benefit of price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth credit weakness is thin tangible asset cover. Goodwill and intangibles exceed shareholders' equity and USD 355.08 million of joint venture notes and equity pays no cash interest, so recovery rests on enterprise value and on partners Griffon does not control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Griffon is a listed manufacturer of residential and commercial garage doors, rolling steel doors and ceiling fans, reported as one operating segment, Building Products, since the AMES tools and garden businesses were sold or closed in FY2026. Revenue was USD 1,848.38 million, of which residential was USD 1,122.21 million and commercial USD 726.17 million, and about 95% is in the United States. Products reach customers through two home-improvement retailers, independent installing dealers and direct-to-consumer fan sales, orders are short cycle, and no backlog is disclosed. Demand is seasonal, with doors strongest in the first and fourth fiscal quarters and fans in the second and third.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For creditors this means cash flow visibility is limited to an order cycle of under a year, so quarterly cash flow and revolver use swing with the season, but the business is capital-light and the exit from the lower-margin AMES businesses left a higher-margin core. That supports debt service and refinancing confidence, at the price of a narrower business that depends on housing activity and two customers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Griffon is a widely held, publicly listed parent with no sponsor or controlling holder identified, employees owning about 8% through the employee stock ownership plan, and no leverage target stated. Its board is independent apart from the chief executive, who has been chairman since 2018. In 2024 it repurchased stock for USD 98.25 million from funds affiliated with Voss Capital, whose chief investment officer had been a director, and the 2025 annual report records an activist campaign begun in 2021. The holder structure beyond that is not established because the proxy statement is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditors hold claims on the operating subsidiaries: six wholly owned domestic subsidiaries guarantee the notes, material domestic subsidiaries guarantee the revolver, and the revolver is secured on substantially all domestic assets, while the notes are unsecured. The two equity-method joint ventures, 43% of Veritage Brands and 49% of Griffon ANZ, are not consolidated, so their own debt is not Griffon's, but Griffon is a creditor of both through paid-in-kind notes. The credit implication is that financial policy is set by a public board that has returned most free cash flow to shareholders, and that sponsor-style extraction is absent while policy discretion is wide.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is cyclical, discretionary and concentrated rather than recurring. Sales into remodeling follow the aging of housing stock and existing home sales, commercial sales follow commercial construction and repair, and purchases of many products are discretionary for consumers. Revenue fell 3.27% in FY2025 and rose 2.95% in FY2026, so it is stable around USD 1.8 billion, but FY2026 growth was price and mix of 6% against volume down 3%. The filing says price increases are hard to pass through quickly when raw material costs rise, and contract duration, renewal rates and switching costs are not disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit implication is that revenue is predictable in level but not in composition: a price-led year can hide weak volume, and the exclusive retailer relationships give volume visibility only as long as both retailers keep the supply arrangement. No customer reached 10% of FY2026 revenue, which limits single-name revenue risk, while the two largest hold 8% and 11% of net receivables.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost of goods was 53.64% of FY2026 revenue and selling, general and administrative expense 23.65%, so gross profit funds a large overhead layer. Galvanized steel is the principal raw material, sourced finished goods were about 10% of revenue and sourced components about 13% of cost of goods, and the fixed and variable split of costs is not printed. Selling, general and administrative expense rose 1.5%, with higher stock compensation and distribution costs, while gross profit rose only 1%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended under mild volume pressure only if price keeps rising, because lower volume absorbs less overhead and raw material costs pass through with a lag. Only 16.75% of the added FY2026 revenue turned into gross profit, against an average margin of 46.36%, which shows how much of the price increase was absorbed. A further volume fall without price would therefore reduce EBITDA faster than revenue, which is the operating leverage that drives the downside case below.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital expenditure of USD 37.91 million was 2.05% of revenue and 0.94x depreciation and amortization, and no split between maintenance and growth spending is printed. Starting from adjusted EBITDA of USD 459.59 million, cash interest of USD 81.08 million, cash taxes of USD 96.04 million and capital expenditure leave USD 244.56 million, against free cash flow of USD 266.95 million; the USD 22.40 million difference is working capital, non-cash stock compensation of USD 30.54 million and other items not analysed separately.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Working capital is seasonal, with receivables of USD 191.17 million and inventories of USD 183.58 million against payables of USD 56.17 million, firm purchase obligations of USD 99.31 million due in fiscal 2027 and operating lease liabilities of USD 67.92 million that sit outside the debt figure. EBITDA converts to durable free cash flow at 58.08% of adjusted EBITDA, which is available for debt service, deleveraging and liquidity, although the board currently sends most of it to shareholders. Pension and retiree medical claims outside debt are small: the Hunter Fan pension plan was terminated and expected fiscal 2027 contributions are USD 1.74 million for supplemental benefits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense, as the filing states. The sectional garage door and commercial rolling steel door industry has several large national manufacturers and many regional ones, and Griffon competes on service, quality, brand, design and price; the fan industry is fragmented and includes retailer house brands such as Hampton Bay and Harbor Breeze, which is why the fan business carries more margin risk and why the FY2025 impairment fell there.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New entrants and substitutes pose a limited threat to doors, where brand recognition and the distribution network are the barriers the filing cites, but retailers import directly from low-cost countries to sell private label products, which caps price. Substitution risk for doors and fans is not discussed in the filings and is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is high and is the most important force for credit. Two retailers buy on an exclusive basis, mass merchandisers have strong negotiating power, and the filing states that losing either of the two would be materially adverse; this limits price realisation and exposes volume to a decision by one buyer. Supplier power is moderate: steel is available from many sources but price swings pass through with a lag, and some products come only from suppliers in China.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Trade policy is the material political factor. Some products and components are sourced from China, a few exclusively, and the filing calls trade actions a continuing risk to the fan business and a smaller risk to Clopay, which manufactures only in the United States. Tariffs can raise the price of China-sourced goods, disrupted customer ordering and contributed to the FY2025 fan impairment, so a further tariff change would hit fan margin first.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The material economic factor is the U.S. housing and commercial property cycle together with consumer credit, because remodeling is discretionary and the filing links 2027 risk to those markets; steel prices are the second economic input. Social and technological factors are not a primary credit driver on these filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths that support credit are stable free cash flow after interest and taxes, a repaired maturity profile to 2031 and 2034, leading garage door brands and exclusive retail supply, and low capital intensity. Weaknesses that constrain credit are a shareholder-friendly financial policy with a large authority, concentration in two retailers and in remodel demand, price-led margin erosion, and thin tangible asset cover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 20, 54, 72–74, 105; calculation C1; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit are retaining more free cash flow for debt repayment, a recovery in existing home sales that restores volume, and monetising the joint venture notes for cash. Threats that could weaken credit are debt-funded buybacks or acquisitions, tariff and steel cost shocks, a loss of retailer business, and weak performance of the joint ventures that owe Griffon paid-in-kind notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow stability is the strongest dimension: operating cash flow stayed between USD 304.87 million and USD 307.79 million for three years and capital needs are low. Financial policy and governance is the weakest dimension and business diversification is also weak, because returns absorbed 96.23% of three-year free cash flow and the business rests on two product families, one segment and two customers. Scale and market position, competitive advantage, cost and capex flexibility, margin stability, refinancing access and liquidity are average: each has a real support, such as brands, distant maturities or USD 324.23 million of liquidity, offset by concentration, margin erosion or covenant-conditional availability.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 54, 72–74, 105; calculation C1; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The trend is mixed. Net leverage fell to 2.12x (2.15x pro forma for repurchases to 2026-11-16), returns fell each year and interest is falling, but adjusted EBITDA margin fell from 25.99% to 24.86% and liquidity fell to USD 324.23 million from USD 584.72 million a year earlier as the revolver was drawn for the refinancing. Key missing datapoints are the covenant test levels, the split of profit between doors and fans, management projections and ratings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-09-30_gff-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 56, 65, 72, 105; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the base case is stable cash generation on a lighter interest bill: run-rate interest is about USD 16.39 million or 20.22% below FY2026 cash interest, there is no material principal due, and the fourth quarter of FY2026 showed improving margin. Headwinds are the discretionary remodel cycle that the filing says may weigh on 2027, tariff and steel cost uncertainty, and the board's capacity to return cash, with USD 544.80 million of authority and a dividend of USD 0.25 per share declared for payment on 2026-12-16. Management gives no quantitative guidance, so the outlook is a reading of drivers and not a forecast.

fields.name: Quote

fields.value: Over three to five years the credit depends on whether free cash flow is used to reduce debt or returned: at the FY2026 pace of retained cash it would take 12.58 years to repay net debt, so deleveraging below the current level needs either lower returns or higher earnings. The revolver matures in 2031 and the notes in 2034, so refinancing becomes the medium-term event, and a stable business with moderate leverage should be able to refinance if it has not re-levered. Sector tailwinds are the aging housing stock and existing home sales cited by management, and company tailwinds are the lower interest cost and the narrower, higher-margin portfolio.

fields.value: The scenario starts with a further volume fall in residential repair and remodel, which is 53.34% of revenue and the most discretionary demand, with retailers resisting further price increases. Assume revenue in that end market falls 10%, which is USD 98.59 million, and that overhead and selling costs do not fall, so the lost gross profit of USD 45.71 million comes straight off EBITDA at the FY2026 gross margin of 46.36%. Reported EBITDA of USD 447.53 million would fall by 10.21% to USD 401.82 million, and after tax at the FY2026 effective rate of 28.21% free cash flow would fall by USD 32.82 million to USD 234.14 million, leaving USD 42.43 million after returns at the FY2026 pace.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On that base, pro forma net leverage would rise from 2.15x to about 2.40x, and to about 3.75x if the whole authority were also debt-funded, which is the combined path that would test the revolver covenants whose levels are not supplied. There would be no liquidity distress from operations alone: liquidity of USD 324.23 million is intact, free cash flow stays positive, run-rate cover stays above 6.21x, and nothing material is due before fiscal 2031. Management levers are the discretionary repurchases, which fell from USD 309.92 million in FY2024 to USD 151.18 million in FY2026, the dividend of USD 40.53 million, capital expenditure of USD 37.91 million and selling costs. Resilience therefore appears sufficient unless financial policy turns the revolver into the funding source for shareholder returns. The primary downside path is a volume decline combined with debt-funded buybacks.

fields.value: Overall, Griffon presents an adequate business profile supported by a leading garage door position, exclusive retailer supply, low capital intensity and stable free cash flow, but credit quality is constrained by concentration in two retailers and remodel demand, price-led margin erosion and a shareholder-friendly financial policy. Cash-flow durability appears strong due to operating cash flow that stayed within a range of USD 2.93 million over three years and capital expenditure of 2.05% of revenue. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the board's restraint on repurchases, the revolver covenant headroom and continued access to the unsecured note market. The primary downside path is a volume decline combined with debt-funded buybacks. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indenture, the split of profit between doors and fans, management projections, ratings and market prices. Top risk: debt-funded shareholder returns on top of weaker volume.
